title.narrative: Operation of the National Blood Bank in Mogadishu (Phase Two)

description.narrative: Contribute to building the health sector infrastructure and localizing services in the region by activating specialized medical centers (National Blood Bank); improve the level of health services provided in the Republic of Somalia and enhance coordination among health facilities to access National Blood Bank services; and contribute to building the capacity of local personnel for storing and transfusing blood to those in need.

Humanitarian response to reduce mortality and morbidity among women, girls, boys, and men affected by the crisis by providing timely, safe, and equitable life-saving humanitarian assistance, and enhancing the resilience of vulnerable women, girls, men, and boys of all ages affected by the crisis through increased safe, dignified, and adequate access to multi-sectoral responses and sustainable solutions.

To improve the level of health services provided in the Federal Republic of Somalia and enhance coordination among health facilities to access national blood bank services; to ensure the availability of safe blood and its components and save the lives of patients in need of blood transfusions; to facilitate the early detection of blood diseases and blood-borne illnesses, while clarifying contraindications to blood donation; to promote, educate, and raise awareness among donors and encourage them to donate blood, highlighting its benefits to their health and their humanitarian service to their community, thus maintaining a sufficient blood bank with all blood types and components; to contribute to building the health sector infrastructure and localizing services in the region by activating specialized medical centers (the national blood bank); and to reduce the number of deaths by ensuring the availability of safe blood units and appropriate components in terms of quality, type, and quantity. In a timely manner, the project aims to reduce the spread of epidemic, infectious, and bloodborne diseases and implement infection control standards; contribute to building the capacity of local personnel through training and education programs, blood donation and care services, and safe methods for storing and transfusing blood to those in need; promote the safe disposal of medical waste; and establish an electronic system by automating data on donors, beneficiaries, and recipients through a database.
